quick.topic: Test your menu with a tree test
quick.summary: How to find out whether people can find things, before any screen is designed.
quick.takeaway: Text only menu, real tasks, see where people go.

parts.title: Test your menu with a tree test

beats.line: Users cannot find invoices. I renamed the menu. How do I know it is better?

board.text: Test your menu with a tree test

beats.line: Run a tree test before you build anything.
Show only the menu as plain text. No colours, no layout.
Give a task. Where would you find last month’s invoice?
Record where each person clicks first, and if they succeed.
Without the real design, is that a fair test?
Fairer. It tests the labels alone, with no visual hints.
Eight of ten went to billing first. The old menu got three.
Now you know the new labels work.

quiz.question: What does a tree test measure?
options: Whether people can find things using the labels and structure alone
quiz.explanation: It shows a text-only structure, so success depends only on the labels and grouping.

quiz.question: A tree test needs finished screen designs to be useful.
quiz.explanation: It uses the menu as plain text, so it can be run before any screen is designed.
